fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: The status page lists 25 incidents from 6 August to 4 November 2026, 22 of them affecting Sandboxes; the longest was 16 hours of unreachable workloads in us-was-1 on 1 September.

incidents.title: Some sandboxes are unavailable in us-was-1

method: Atlassian Statuspage v2 /api/v2/incidents.json on status.blaxel.ai (25 records, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-03, all inside the window). Affected components read from each incident page /incidents/<id> (embedded RSC payload, matched to /api/v2/components.json names). Durations = resolved_at minus created_at.
gaps: Incident pages are client-rendered; titles and affected components were read from the server HTML (<title> and the embedded payload), not from rendered text.
One incident (10 Oct 2026, "Elevated sandbox creation failures in us-was-1") lists no affected component.
Regions appear only in titles; there is no region component, so the us-was-1/us-pdx-1 split comes from incident names.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: No incident history is published: the status page shows per-component uptime and latency over a rolling 90-day window, so individual outages cannot be looked up.

countNote: No dated incident list exists to count. The separate machine-readable /incidents.json holds 344 automatic probe-failure records in the window (41 outage, 303 degraded), all on Box Stop + Resume, Box Fork, Box Creation, Ascii API, Box Dashboard, Box Desktop Streaming and Box SSH; the page does not render them and they have no titles.
method: status.ascii.dev rendered HTML plus its script.js (which loads only status.json and history.json), then /history.json and /incidents.json read directly. Count of curated incidents: none published.
gaps: The page shows uptime blocks and latency metrics per component; it has no incident list, no incident titles and no dated outage entries.

/incidents.json is served but not linked or rendered by the page; its entries are probe failures (e.g. a 174-hour run of the 'Box Stop + Resume (extreme edge cases suite)' probe from 6 to 13 August), not customer-facing incident reports, so they are not reported as incidents.
Retention is 90 days (retentionDays: 90), so nothing older than the window exists to compare against.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: The status page lists 58 incidents naming Workers, Containers or Durable Objects from 6 August to 4 November 2026; the longest was a 56-hour Workers Cron Triggers degradation from 9 to 12 September.

source.quote: Workers Cron Triggers degraded Started Sep 9, 2026, 19:17 UTC Resolved Sep 12, 2026, 03:34 UTC

incidents.title: Issues with Workers Build failing to start

method: Cloudflare Status API v3 /api/v3/history?type=incident&per_page=25, paged by cursor from 2026-11-04 back to 2026-07-31 (11 pages, 275 records, no duplicates). 258 incidents start in the window; 58 of those name Workers, Containers, Sandbox or Durable Objects. Scheduled maintenance (type=maintenance) excluded. Durations = resolved_at minus starts_at.
gaps: The documented v2 /api/v2/incidents.json returns only the 50 most recent incidents, which reaches back only to 19 October; the v3 history endpoint used here is the one the status page's own History view calls.

There is no 'Sandbox' component or incident; the sandbox-relevant entries are the two Containers incidents ('Cloudflare Container Issues', 3 Nov, 1h 11m; 'Unable to start containers in Asia-Pacific', 21 Sep, 41m) plus any incident whose affected components include Containers.
Counts by component are component appearances across those 58 incidents (Durable Objects 25, Workers 11, Workers Builds 9, Containers 8), not incident totals.
All times are UTC as published.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: The status page lists six incident notices from 6 August to 4 November 2026; the oldest is a CEPH storage degradation posted on 8 September with a published estimate of 900 minutes.

source.quote: 08.09.2026 11:00 am (UTC+1) Degraded Performance - CEPH Cluster: non-critical Estimated duration: 900 minutes

incidents.title: Degraded Performance - CEPH Cluster: non-critical
incidents.duration: not published; estimate 900 minutes; last update 2026-10-14T12:28Z
incidents.component: Object Storage / CEPH cluster (APAC after 14 Oct)

incidents.title: Patching of internal systems (CVE-2026-98432)
incidents.component: Webspace, network boot, DNS resolvers, blog, backup servers

method: Single-page status list at contabo-status.com read with Context.dev web_scrape (markdown) and curl, cross-checked against its Atom feed /rss (rss.php). Six entries with ids 226, 225, 224, 223, 221, 213. Start times converted from the page's (UTC+1) labels; update times taken from the feed's timestamps.
gaps: No incident archive and no end times: entries are edited in place and only the six current ones are published, so an incident that was closed and removed before 4 November would not appear. The count is what the page lists today, not a guaranteed 90-day total.
The 26 October 'unauthorized access' notice named in the brief is not on the status page; the 26 October entry is an Object Storage disruption and is counted. Nothing was excluded.
Per-incident URLs (/226 etc.) return a domain-parking 404; permalinks are the #id anchors on the main page.
Durations are only published for one entry, as an estimate (900 minutes); the rest have start times and update times but no end.

Times are the page's local labels marked (UTC+1), while the feed's <updated> stamps carry +02:00 for October, so late-October starts may be an hour off in UTC. Durations are unaffected: no end times exist.

fact.label: Recent incidents
fact.value: The status page lists 15 incidents from 6 August to 4 November 2026; the most severe was the Cloud Control Panel and API case on 24 August, whose postmortem counts 3.5 hours of elevated errors across the API and control panel.

source.quote: Between 16:56 UTC and 23:09 UTC on August 24, 2026, customers using DigitalOcean’s Cloud Control Panel, Public API, and dependent product management systems experienced elevated request error rates, peaking at 25%, in two distinct windows totaling 3.5 hours of active degradation within a 6-hour span.

incidents.title: Cloud Control Panel and API
incidents.duration: 25h 49m open; postmortem counts 3.5h of active degradation

method: Atlassian Statuspage v2 /api/v2/incidents.json on status.digitalocean.com (50 most recent, 2026-04-28 to 2026-11-03, so the window is fully covered); filtered to created_at between 2026-08-06 and 2026-11-04. Components and durations from the same JSON.
gaps: Four of the 15 resolved within the same second they started (0m), which looks like imported or backfilled entries rather than live incidents: 'Multiple Services Availability' (6 Aug), 'Volume Attach/Detach events in FRA1' (13 Aug), 'A Network Disruption in BLR1 Region Impacted Multiple Products' (3 Oct) and 'App Platform Deployments' (13 Oct). They are counted as listed.
The 50-record API cap is not reached inside the window, so no pagination gap.
The widest incident was 'Major Service Interruption in MKC1' (19 Aug, critical, 8h 24m), which affected more components than the two 9-11 hour entries above but was shorter.
